segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
They fought against it for forty days,
and those within were defeated.
And some of the magnates of the city went out,
and received a promise of safety for their lives from the Khan.
And all those warriors embarked in boats,
and fled down the river.
And the Khan took control of the city,
and he did not harm anyone in it.
And from there he began to penetrate into those countries.
Now the king of the Cathayans,
the one who was called Altan Khan, that is,
'the Golden King',
gathered his army, one hundred thousand seasoned men,
and sent them to confront the Tatars.
And when they arrived, they surrounded the Tatars like a ring,
because they were very mighty.
Now when the Khan saw their strength,
he made use of another stratagem:
he commanded the sorcerers and enchanters who were with him to bring out the rain-stone.
And when they brought it out,

and performed their rituals for three days and three nights, heavy rains and violent downpours began to fall upon the Cathayans, together with severe snow, cold, and frost, in the days of Tammuz (July).
Then the Tatars, like wolves that tear sheep to pieces,
tore the Cathayans to pieces,
and crushed them with a terrible defeat.
Then Altan Khan fled to his royal city,
and gathered his wives, his children, his brothers, and all his kinsmen into his palace.
And he commanded all his servants,
and they heaped up many piles of wood,
and set fire to them,
and he and all those belonging to him were burned.
And the armies of the Mongols came,
and plundered that city, which was called Namking {OCR? / Nanjing / Zhongdu}, and many other cities;
and they killed many in them,
and took countless desirable and handsome boys and girls as captives.
And so the Khan returned from there with great joy,
and reached the mountains of Karakorum,
and built a city,
and called it Ordu-Balik, that is,
'the City of the Camp';
today, however, it is known as the city of Karakorum.
And he brought craftsmen and inhabitants to it from the land of the Cathayans and from the lands of the Arabs (Muslims),
and settled them in it.
And while the Khan was occupied with the joy of the victory that had been granted to him,
his younger brother Tolui passed away,
the one who was very much beloved...
